newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hochtief overseas units led growth in 96.
newsitem.headline: Hochtief overseas units led growth in 96.

text.p: German construction group Hochtief AG said on Tuesday its international activities drove growth in orders and output in 1996.
Overseas business contributed 50 percent of orders in 1996, up from a 44 percent share the year before.
As previously announced, orders totalled 14.32 billion marks ($8.3 billion) and output 12.18 billion marks last year.
International orders rose 37 percent to 7.1 billion marks and overseas output increased 25.3 percent to 4.96 billion marks, chief executive Han-Peter Keitel said at a news conference.
German orders rose 9.9 percent to 7.22 billion marks. Output in Germany, where price competition has been fierce, was up only 1.6 percent to 7.22 billion marks, Keitel said.
Growth outside of Germany was led by its Dutch and Australian units, he said.
In the Netherlands, Ballast Nedam saw output rise 27 percent to 3.4 billion marks, while operating profit was unchanged at 81.2 million marks.
Leighton Holdings in Australia in 1996 had a record year with revenue rising 24 percent to 3.1 billion marks and profit climbing 37 percent to 93.9 million marks.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.727 German Marks)
